questions.q: What are the two phases of the design loop described in the summary?
a: Widening with many ideas, then narrowing to a few
Testing with customers, then launching the product
Writing a full plan, then raising the money
Interviewing experts, then copying their model
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the first phase is like brainstorming and the second narrows the options down.

questions.q: Which tool does the author recommend for mapping opportunities, risks and resources?
a: The Business Model Canvas
The Value Proposition Canvas
The customer journey map
The four-quadrant SWOT grid
questions.why: Lesson 1 credits the author’s own canvas with laying out opportunities, risks and needed resources.

questions.q: What does the summary say a business concept really is?
a: An assumption that has to be tested
A promise that has to be kept
A plan that only needs funding
A hunch that experience replaces
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that however bright the future looks, your concept remains an assumption.

questions.q: How should assumptions be written so they can be tested properly?
a: With specific numbers, names and time frames
As broad goals covering the whole market
As open questions for friends and family
As short statements of the company vision
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends precise hypotheses such as a set number of sales by a given date.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a discovery experiment?
a: To learn whether your concept is right and where to improve
To prove a finished product to potential investors
To confirm a decision you have already made
To measure sales after a full market launch
questions.why: Lesson 3 says discovery experiments yield insights that show if an idea is on track or not.
